title: Detroit: Become Human
japaneseTitle: デトロイト ビカム ヒューマン
composer: Philip Sheppard, Nima Fakhrara, John Paesano
shortDescription: Quantic Dream's ambitious branching interactive narrative exploring artificial intelligence sentience and civil rights across near-future Detroit.
historicalSignificance: The most technologically elaborate interactive narrative drama in video game history, featuring a transparent post-chapter flowchart revealing thousands of branching moral choices and selling over 10 million copies.

editorialContent.overview: Set in the year 2038 where humanoid androids handle all societal labor, the narrative weaves together three distinct synthetic protagonists: Connor (a police investigator hunting rogue 'deviants'), Kara (a domestic caretaker who flees with a young child), and Markus (an activist leading an android liberation movement).
editorialContent.gameplay: Combines scene investigation, dialogue negotiation, moral crisis decision-trees, and time-sensitive contextual action prompts with permanent character death consequences.
editorialContent.technicalInnovation: Constructed an enormous script exceeding 4,000 pages of branching logic, tracked transparently through visual end-of-chapter flowcharts, and recorded via hundreds of motion-captured actors.
editorialContent.culturalImpact: Demonstrated that interactive branching storytelling can achieve blockbuster mainstream success without traditional combat systems.
editorialContent.preservationNotes: Preserved on PS4 disc media and ported to PC with 4K resolution support.

awards: Game Critics Awards Best Action/Adventure Nominee

technicalSpecs.soundChip: Three independent composers creating bespoke character scores
